record.original_question: Let a term-rewriting system, or more generally a system with bound variables, be finitely generated, full in the sense that its terms are all terms generated from its function symbols, and Church-Rosser. Must it have a recursive one-step reduction strategy that always reaches a normal form when one exists?

evidence.quote: Has any full, finitely-generated and Church-Rosser term-rewriting system (or system with bound variables) a recursive, one-step, normalizing reduction strategy?

artifact.status_search_result: This question (Kennaway's Open Problem 10 in the RTA list) was resolved negatively: a full, finitely generated, Church-Rosser (in fact left- and right-linear) term rewriting system has been constructed which admits no computable one-step normalizing strategy. Positive answers are known under additional restrictions (e.g., strongly sequential regular systems, or systems with the recursively acyclic Church-Rosser property).

status_evidence.title: A Confluent Rewriting System Having No Computable, One-Step, Normalizing Strategy
status_evidence.snippet: A full and finitely generated Church-Rosser term rewriting system is presented that has no computable one-step, normalizing strategy; the system is both left- and right-linear. The result provides a negative answer to Kennaway's 1989 question (RTA Open Problem 10).
status_evidence.claim: The problem has been answered negatively.

status_evidence.title: RTA List of Open Problems - Summary
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems in rewriting, including problem 10 posed by Kennaway (1989) on existence of recursive one-step normalizing strategies for full finitely-generated Church-Rosser systems.
status_evidence.claim: Identifies the problem as RTA Open Problem 10.

status_evidence.title: Reduction Strategies and Acyclicity
status_evidence.snippet: For every recursive strongly sequential regular term rewrite system there is a recursive normalising one-step strategy; extended to systems with the recursively acyclic Church-Rosser property.
status_evidence.claim: Positive partial results exist for restricted subclasses.
